items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I became quite friendly with Adelaide Hall

ctx.x: I’m thinking earlier still. Just as you’re starting your . . . into a professional career, moving from being at the Guildhall to now you’re starting to look beyond that and at an early stage of your professional career.

It’s so funny. I don’t remember having that many . . . what I would call jazz friends. I became quite friendly with Adelaide Hall, and she had a pianist, an accompanist, who wrote . . . now I’m having a problem remembering his name. You would know it if I said it. He wrote all . . . Oh, this is terrible. He was somebody I admired a lot. He wrote all these . . . they were . . . I guess you could call them novelty piano. They were really good. “Dodging a Divorcee” was one. Oh, I can’t think of his name [Reginald…
